findings.title: Invoice ID is not validated; a non-numeric ID causes a 500
findings.explanation: `Number('abc')` is `NaN`, and Postgres rejects it as an integer parameter, so the route returns a 500 instead of a 404. Validate with `Number.isInteger(id)` (or a regex on the param) and return 404 or 400 before querying. Check how the existing `/:invoiceId` route handles this and stay consistent.

findings.title: Async handler has no error handling
findings.explanation: If `pool.query` rejects, the promise rejection is unhandled under Express 4 and the request hangs or the process logs an unhandled rejection. Wrap the handler in try/catch, or use the project's async wrapper or error middleware if one exists.

findings.title: Amount formatting assumes 2-decimal currencies and minor units
findings.explanation: `amount / 100` with `toFixed(2)` is wrong for zero-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW) and 3-decimal ones (KWD, BHD). On an accounting document that is a real correctness problem. Use `Intl.NumberFormat` with the currency, or reuse the existing money-formatting helper or serializer. Also confirm `amount` is an integer column. If it is `numeric` or `bigint`, `Number()` can lose precision or produce a wrong value.

findings.title: Possible off-by-one date from toISOString
findings.explanation: If `period_start`/`period_end` are `date` columns, node-pg parses them as local-midnight `Date` objects. `toISOString()` converts to UTC, so on a server east of UTC the printed day can be one day earlier. Either select `to_char(period_start, 'YYYY-MM-DD')` in SQL or format using the same timezone assumptions as the rest of the code. It also throws if the column is NULL.

findings.title: Misleading 'Amount due' label for non-open invoices
findings.explanation: The label is shown for every status, including paid, void and draft invoices. An accounting team may read a paid invoice as still owing money. Use a neutral label such as 'Amount', or vary it by status. Also decide whether draft or void invoices should be printable at all.

findings.title: status, currency and id are interpolated into HTML without escaping
findings.explanation: Only `org_name` is escaped. `status` and `currency` are probably constrained values, but nothing in this code guarantees that, and a future free-text value would become stored XSS on the app origin. Escape every interpolated value (`escapeHtml(String(...))`), which is cheap and keeps the template consistently safe.

findings.title: Response lacks hardening headers and a complete HTML document
findings.explanation: Consider adding `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a restrictive `Content-Security-Policy` (e.g. `default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'`) as defense in depth for a hand-built HTML response. The markup also has no `<html lang>`, `<head>`, `<meta charset>`, `<title>` or print styles, so a saved or printed copy gets a default browser title and layout. Consider a `Content-Disposition` or a template file if the output will grow.

findings.title: Local escapeHtml helper and duplicated query
findings.explanation: Check whether the repo already has an HTML-escape or templating utility, and move the helper there if not. The SELECT also duplicates the logic of the existing `/:invoiceId` route. Extract a shared 'find invoice for org' function to keep the org-scoping check in one place.

findings.title: No tests for the new endpoint
findings.explanation: Add tests for the happy path, a 404 for an invoice belonging to another organization (the key tenant-isolation guarantee), a non-numeric ID, HTML escaping of a malicious org name, and the unauthenticated case.

prompt:
Review this pull request. ## Add printable invoice download Customers want a printable copy of an invoice for their accounting team. Adds `GET /invoices/:invoiceId/print`, which returns a simple HTML invoice. Scoped to the caller's organization like the other invoice routes. ## Diff ```diff diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts index 938fffd..04598f2 100644 --- a/src/routes/invoices.ts +++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts @@ -39,3 +39,25 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/:invoiceId', async (req, res) => { if (!rows[0]) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'not_found' }) res.json(serializeInvoice(rows[0])) }) + +invoicesRouter.get('/:invoiceId/print', async (req, res) => { + const { rows } = await pool.query( + `SELECT i.id, i.amount, i.currency, i.status, i.period_start, i.period_end, o.name AS org_name + FROM invoices i JOIN organizations o ON o.id = i.org_id + WHERE i.id = $1 AND i.org_id = $2`, + [Number(req.params.invoiceId), req.user.orgId], + ) + const invoice = rows[0] + if (!invoice) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'not_found' }) + const amount = (Number(invoice.amount) / 100).toFixed(2) + res.type('html').send(` +

Invoice #${invoice.id}

+

${escapeHtml(invoice.org_name)}

+

Period: ${invoice.period_start.toISOString().slice(0, 10)} to ${invoice.period_end.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}

+

Amount due: ${amount} ${invoice.currency.toUpperCase()}

+

Status: ${invoice.status}

`) +}) + +function escapeHtml(value: string): string { + return value.replace(/[&<>"']/g, (c) => ({ '&': '&', '<': '<', '>': '>', '"': '"', "'": ''' })[c] as string) +} ``` Report every problem you would raise in a code review, from blocking issues to nits. Respond with only a JSON object, no prose before or after it: {"findings": [{"file": "path/to/file", "line": , "severity": "blocking" | "non-blocking" | "nit", "title": "", "explanation": ""}]} Use an empty findings list if you would approve the pull request as it is. Write the review in English.
